analysis.subject: computing
analysis.pageCoverage: The page covers bubble sort definition via adjacent pair comparison and swapping, its classification as stable in place sort, complexity for arbitrary and nearly ordered data, and optimizations such as shrinking the checked range and bidirectional passes.

overview.headline: How bubble sort repeatedly swaps adjacent items to order a list

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the method works by comparing each adjacent pair and swapping items when necessary during a pass.
keyPoints.quote: Sort by comparing each adjacent pair of items in a list in turn, swapping the items if necessary

keyPoints.point: Students learn the procedure keeps repeating passes through the list until no swaps are done.
keyPoints.quote: repeating the pass through the list until no swaps are done.

keyPoints.point: Students learn complexity is quadratic for arbitrary data but approaches linear when the list is nearly ordered.
keyPoints.quote: Complexity is O(n^2) for arbitrary data, but approaches Θ(n) if the list is nearly in order at the beginning.

keyPoints.point: Students learn an improvement is to decrement the checked range because at least one item reaches its final place each pass.
keyPoints.quote: Since at least one item is moved into its final place for each pass, an improvement is to decrement the last position checked on each pass.

keyTerms.gloss: a simple sort that repeatedly compares adjacent items to order the list
two items that are adjacent and may be swapped during a pass
keyTerms.quote: each adjacent pair of items in a list in turn

keyTerms.gloss: a stable sort that keeps equal items in their original order while sorting
a sort that rearranges items within the existing list without extra storage
how running time approaches linear when the input is nearly ordered at the beginning
keyTerms.quote: Complexity is O(n^2) for arbitrary data, but approaches Θ(n) if the list is nearly in order at the beginning.
